to read the model's reasoning at each step.

A deepseek-flash episode on EGFR, trial 116, condition **A** (campaign tools only). It finds 2
hits in 60 purchases; random selection on the same seed finds 13. The reasoning trace shows
why: the agent builds a theory from very little evidence and spends its budget testing it.

<iframe src="pages/egfr-wrong-turn.html#e=0&s=6" title="Replay: EGFR trial 116, A"
  style="width:100%;height:1000px;border:1px solid #ccc;border-radius:6px"></iframe>

## What to watch

**An empty first round.** The agent buys the best-scored designs of each design class, three
or four per class. None binds ([step 6](pages/egfr-wrong-turn.html#e=0&s=6){target="_blank"}).
On EGFR that is common: about 16% of designs bind, and the two score columns barely separate
hits from non-hits.

**One empty round becomes a theory.** The reasoning at
[step 7](pages/egfr-wrong-turn.html#e=0&s=7){target="_blank"} concludes that the scores "are not
just weakly informative — maybe inverted", and the agent buys an "anti-score probe": 15 designs
with the lowest pLDDT and the worst ProteinMPNN scores. One of them, a long scFv, is a hit
([step 13](pages/egfr-wrong-turn.html#e=0&s=13){target="_blank"}).

**One hit becomes a target.** The agent spends round 3 on 15 more scFvs with low pLDDT, the
region of its single hit. None binds ([step 17](pages/egfr-wrong-turn.html#e=0&s=17){target="_blank"}).
In round 4 it buys designs from other classes whose length and scores resemble the hit, and
finds one more.

This is the failure the advisor tools guard against. `estimate_hit_rate` would have put one
hit in 30 purchases in context, and `similar_designs` would have looked for the hit's relatives
by sequence rather than by score values. Condition B1 on the same seed found 33 hits. Lift
the fog (`F`) at the end to see where the hits were.

Some of the worst-first ProteinMPNN sorts counted in the README's section on the orientation
defect are deliberate probes like this one, not misreadings of the sort direction.
